public_rationale: Marcus offers a qualified inference: xAI apparently omitted checks or performed them poorly. Scoring it as a firm assertion would remove that qualification, while scoring poor performance would require an adequacy standard he did not supply. Contemporary reporting describes missing public results, and a later model card documents evaluations. Neither establishes the full assessment as true or false. The narrower disclosure question is checkable, but substituting it would change the claim.
limitations: This disposition does not endorse or reject xAI’s safety practices.
The later model card cannot establish July pre-release practice without dated testing records.

our_interpretation: The statement is a qualified inference about xAI’s pre-release safety practices, not an unqualified assertion that no testing occurred.
The supplied context associates this criticism with the July 2025 Grok release controversy. The quoted words do not themselves specify Grok 4.
Missing public documentation can establish a disclosure gap. It cannot by itself establish that internal testing was absent or poorly performed.
Marcus supplies no standard for what counts as performing these checks poorly. Assigning one would materially change the assessment.
criteria.support_condition: No binary support condition faithfully tests the complete qualified assessment as written. Records of omitted checks or documented failures against a specified safety standard could substantiate its factual basis.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No binary contradiction condition faithfully tests the complete assessment as written. Dated records of adequate pre-release testing could weaken the inference, but the existence of some testing alone would not refute the alternative that it was performed poorly.

evidence.explanation: This contemporary report describes a public disclosure gap, not proof that testing was absent or inadequate. News reporting is used because no primary admission of the disclosure gap was obtained.

The later model card documents evaluations and mitigations, limiting any suggestion that xAI never evaluated Grok 4. Its description of current methods does not establish the adequacy of checks before the July release.
